answer: A bonded-escrow protocol deters sybil attacks by linking correlated equivocation across k identities: the penalty grows as O(k²), rather than treating each signer in isolation. Detection can also trigger asymmetric capital depreciation, so a coordinated swarm loses an exponentially larger share of its bonded stake than a lone violator. A whisper of coordination may be hard to prove, but juniper-tagged attestations expose shared control; at the nadir, the swarm’s remaining collateral may be negligible.
